- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for sudden drop in sentiment and reduce forecast slope accordingly.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag true price movements by 2–5 days; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for early days, then adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underperforms; use sentiment as a proxy for volatility: if sentiment >0.5, add 0.5–1% to forecast; if <0.5, subtract 0.5–1%.
